unit.title: Reading CVC Words and Simple Sentences

contentBlocks.text: Last year you blended your first word: sat. This year we'll get much stronger at reading whole words — starting with a quick warm-up on short-A words like the ones you already know.

Words like sat, mat, cat, and hat all follow the same pattern: consonant-vowel-consonant, or 'CVC' for short. Practice reading each one by blending the sounds: c-a-t, cat. m-a-t, mat. h-a-t, hat. Once you can blend these smoothly, try reading them faster, like a real reader — not sound by sound, but as a whole word.
You just read four real words fluently! This CVC pattern shows up in hundreds of words you'll learn to read this year.

objectives: Read short-A CVC words (sat, mat, cat, hat) by blending sounds smoothly
Recognize the consonant-vowel-consonant (CVC) pattern as a recurring, decodable word structure
materialsNeeded: Optional: letter cards for S, M, A, T, C, H
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review the short A sound and the letters S, M, T from last year briefly.
2. Introduce two new letters if needed: C (sound /k/) and H (sound /h/).
3. Model blending each CVC word slowly, then faster: c-a-t... cat.
4. Practice all four words (sat, mat, cat, hat) together, aiming for smooth, whole-word reading by the end.
5. Move to the worksheet: read and trace each word.
6. Close by asking the child to use one word in a spoken sentence.
differentiationTips: Struggling: slow back down to sound-by-sound blending rather than pushing for fluent whole-word reading yet
Ready for more: ask the child to think of one more short-A CVC word not on the list (bat, rat, fat)
For a child who reads these words instantly already, have them use each word in a full spoken sentence
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a reading and tracing-practice activity — check that the child can blend and read each CVC word, not just trace it silently.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Fluent CVC word reading is the foundational Grade 1 phonics-based decoding skill (the course's stated focus) that everything else this week — new patterns, digraphs, and sentence reading — builds directly on.

generationData.instructions: Read each word by blending its sounds, trace it, then write it once more on your own.
